html:
English settlers from nearby St Kitts began farming Anguilla in 1650. The island had earlier been home to Amerindian peoples related to the Taino.

The soil was thin and rain was scarce, so big sugar estates never took hold as they did on Barbados or St Kitts. Many settlers and freed people became small farmers, fishermen, sailors and salt rakers instead.

From the 1820s London ran Anguilla through St Kitts. That tie, which most Anguillans resented, led in the end to the Anguilla Revolution of 1967 and a separate place in the British Empire.
